“You can borrow my phone if you want,” Hansa said. “Only for the photos. Not the messages.”
Mehak blinked. “Wow. Since when?”
“Since you kept every secret for six months. I trust you more than I did in January.”
“You said never touch your phone.”
“I did. Rules can grow. But the messages stay private, and the diary stays in my bag. Those are still mine.”
“Fair.” Mehak scrolled the gallery. “I'm not going to open anything else.”
“I know. That's why I said yes.” Hansa took a sip of her lemonade. “If it ever feels wrong, I'll tell you and take it back.”
“Deal.”

qa.a: The messages stay private, and the diary stays in Hansa's bag.

qa.q: Why did Hansa change her rule, and how does she feel about Mehak?
qa.a: Hansa trusts Mehak more, since Mehak kept every secret for six months.

qa.q: What could Hansa do if the arrangement stops feeling right?
qa.a: Hansa could tell Mehak and take the permission back, as she says, while keeping the core limits.

qa.q: How might Mehak feel about the change?
qa.a: Mehak may feel surprised and trusted, and careful not to open anything beyond the gallery.

grounding: After months of trust, a teen adjusts what she shares with a close friend but keeps her core limits, showing that boundaries can shift with time.

passage: When Anirban and I started talking in Class 9, I had rules. No sharing my location. No talking about why I left my old school. No photos that weren't group ones. I'm Vandana, and back then I barely knew him. Eight months later, things were different. He had sat with me on the steps the day I cried over my results and never told a soul. He'd kept every small secret I'd tested him with. So one Sunday I sat down with my old list and changed it. I told him about my old school, properly, for the first time. I turned on location sharing for our walks back from tuition, just for those evenings. But some lines stayed exactly where they were: no private photos, no passwords. Looking back, the list didn't disappear. It just grew a little in the places he'd earned.

qa.q: What did Vandana turn on for the walks back from tuition?
qa.a: Vandana turned on location sharing for those evenings.

qa.q: How did Vandana feel about Anirban after eight months?
qa.a: Vandana felt trusting and safe, because Anirban had kept every small secret and stayed kind on a hard day.

qa.q: What else could Vandana do to keep the new sharing comfortable?
qa.a: Vandana could look at the list again every few months and switch location sharing off whenever it stops feeling right, since the change was a choice, not a demand.

qa.q: How might Anirban experience being trusted with more?
qa.a: Anirban may feel valued that the trust was earned over time, while learning that some limits stay no matter how close they become.

grounding: Shows a teen adjusting what is shared with a close friend after months of trust, while keeping the core limits on photos and passwords.

passage:
Counsellor's note, 12 March.
Chandrika came in today for a follow-up. In October, new to the school, she had made a list with me: what she shares, and with whom. She had kept Sarita, her bench-mate, at arm's length then.
Today she said things had changed. Over five months, Sarita had kept every confidence and never pushed when Chandrika said "not yet." So Chandrika has decided to tell her about her parents' separation and to let her read her poetry notebook. I asked what stays the same. She answered without hesitating: no sharing passwords, and no photos of her posted without asking. She seemed calm, even a little proud, as she crossed out two lines and left the rest.
Next step: a check-in after the term exams, only if she wants one.

qa.q: When had Chandrika first made the list?
qa.a: In October, when she was new to the school.

qa.q: How did Chandrika seem while updating the list?
qa.a: Chandrika seemed calm and a little proud, sure about what to change and what to keep.

qa.q: What would help Chandrika keep the updated list working?
qa.a: She could keep reviewing it at her own pace, and if Sarita ever pushes on a line that stayed, treat that as a reason to slow the new sharing.

qa.q: How might Sarita feel about being told about the separation?
qa.a: Sarita may feel trusted and valued, since the new sharing comes after months of being reliable.

grounding: Illustrates a teen widening what she shares with a close friend after months of trust while keeping her core limits, as observed by a counsellor.
